name: Forgotten Cron on a 12-Year-Old Host
description: A finance close-of-day cron job has been running on RH6-FIN-CRON-01 since 2013. The box is past EOL, was supposed to be retired in 2021, was forgotten, and tonight its disk finally gives up — the close fails for the first time in nine years.
reasoning: An ancient host, a cron service running on it, and a downstream Postgres data warehouse. The simulation models the moment the legacy job stops emitting heartbeats, with cascade impact on a finance pipeline that nobody knew was downstream.

narrative.text: Quiet baseline. Cron hasn't missed a beat in nine years.
Disk smartd warning on RH6-FIN-CRON-01 (it's been firing all week, nobody is on the alias).
Cron job starts: 'Cannot create temp file: input/output error'.
Output file never lands; etl-loader waits, then fails its scheduled pull.
Finance reports a missing entry in tonight's close. Trail leads back to the dead disk.
Job migrated by hand to a modern Linux VM; data backfilled from /var/log/cron's last known good tmpfile.
Close completes ~3 hours late; long-overdue retirement of RH6-FIN-CRON-01 scheduled.
Steady state. Action item: every cron job needs a heartbeat to a central monitor.
